_policy: Quarantined stories still RUN and are still REPORTED, but their failures do
not turn the storybook-probe job red. Quarantine is a stopgap for a story
whose flakiness is understood but not yet fixed — never a parking lot.
Rules enforced by scripts/probe-stories.mjs, which refuses to run if broken:
- at most `maxEntries` stories may be quarantined at once;
- every entry needs `id`, `reason` and an ISO `expires` date;
- on and after `expires` the entry stops shielding the story, so the job
goes red again and someone has to fix, delete or consciously renew it.
A quarantined story that passes is reported as READY so it can be removed.
`a11yEntries` does the same for ONE axe rule on one story (`id` "*" means
every story): the violation is still printed, it just does not gate. Same
cap (`maxA11yEntries`), same required reason and expiry. Only `critical`
and `serious` violations gate in the first place — lowering that threshold
instead of quarantining a rule is not an option, because it silences every
_failure: `failure: "probe-timeout"` marks a story that fails by sitting at the per-story
deadline. Such a story must also carry the `nightly` tag: the per-commit probe
refuses to run otherwise, because two minutes a push on a story that cannot
gate there is the one cost quarantine must not hide.
